\title{Finiteness of the extension of Q generated by Frobenius traces in finite characteristic}
\author{Pierre Deligne}
\date{}
\maketitle

\begin{center}
\textit{Dedie a the memoire of I.~M.~Gelfand}
\end{center}

\noindent\textbf{Resume.} Let $Z_0$ a scheme of type finite on $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $\mathcal{F}_0$ a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf on $Z_0$. We montrons that there exists a extension of type finite $E \subset \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that the factors local of the function $L$ of $\mathcal{F}_0$ let all with coefficients in $E$. Si $Z_0$ is normal connected and that $\mathcal{F}_0$ is a systeme local $\ell$-adique irreducible, of which the determinant is of ordre finite, one can prendre for $E$ a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}$.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Abstract.} Let $\mathcal{F}_0$ be a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf one has scheme $Z_0$ of finite type over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We show the existence of a finite type extension $E \subset \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, such that all local factors of the $L$-function of $\mathcal{F}_0$ have coefficients in $E$. When $Z_0$ is normal and connected, and $\mathcal{F}_0$ an irreducible $\ell$-adic local system whose determinant is of finite order, $E$ can be taken to be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}$.

\section*{0. Introduction}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{0. Introduction}

\subsection*{0.0}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{0.0}

Fixons the notations suivantes:

$\mathbb{F}_q$: a finite field a $q$ elements, of caracteristique $p$;

$\mathbb{F}$: a algebraic closure of $\mathbb{F}_q$;

$\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$: the extension of degree $n$ of $\mathbb{F}_q$ in $\mathbb{F}$;

$W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$: the under-group $\mathbb{Z}$ of $\Gal(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_{q^n}) = \hat{\mathbb{Z}}$ generated by the Frobenius geometric $F$ (the inverse of $x \mapsto x^{q^n}$);

$\ell$: a nombre prime other that $p$;

$\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$: a algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$.

A object on $\mathbb{F}_q$ will be affecte of a indice $0$, and the suppression of this indice indiquera the extension of the field of base of $\mathbb{F}_q$ a $\mathbb{F}$.

For a resume of the formalism of the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves, and of celui of the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves of Weil, I refer to [De2] 1.1.1 and 1.1.10.

Let $\bar{X}_0$ a curve projective smooth and absolument irreducible on $\mathbb{F}_q$, $S_0$ a set finite of points fermes of $\bar{X}_0$ and $X_0 := \bar{X}_0 - S_0$. One notera $K_0$ the field of functions rationnelles on $X_0$ and $A$ the ring of ses adeles.

\subsection*{0.1}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{0.1}

Lafforgue [L] fournit a bijection natural between

(A) Classes of isomorphie of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves of Weil smooth irreductibles of rank $r$ on $X_0$, and

(B) Representations automorphes cuspidales $\pi$ of $GL(r,A)$, not ramifiees en dehors of $S_0$.

This bijection is caracterisee by the equality en each point closed $x_0$ of $X_0$ of factors local of functions $L$ attached to the objects (A) and (B).

In (B), the notion of representation automorphe cuspidale is purement algebraic: one can prendre as field of coefficients n'importe quel field $k$ algebriquement clos of caracteristique $0$. One prend $k = \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. The topologie of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ ne joue aucun role.

Si $Z_0$ is a scheme of type finite on $\mathbb{F}_q$, the action on $\mathbb{F}$ of $W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q)$ induces a action of this group of Weil on $Z = Z_0 \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q} \mathbb{F}$. A $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil $\mathcal{F}_0$ on $Z_0$ is a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $Z$, equipped with a action of $W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q)$ on $(Z,\mathcal{F})$ relevant son action on $Z$. The notion of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf is defined by passage a the limite a partir of celle of sheaf étale of $\mathcal{O}_\lambda/I$-module, for $\mathcal{O}_\lambda$ the cloture integral of $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$ in a finite extension $E_\lambda \subset \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ of $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$, and $I$ a power of the ideal maximal. The topologie of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ joue ici a role crucial. A consequence surprenante of the equivalence between (A) and (B) is that, in the cas of the sheaves smooth semi-simples on the curves, this role is illusoire.

\subsection*{0.2}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{0.2}

One prendra garde that Lafforgue assumed choisi a isomorphism $\iota: \mathbb{C} \xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$, and the utilise for comparer plutot representations automorphes to the sens classique (field of coefficients $\mathbb{C}$) and $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves. Si one utilise the isomorphism $\iota$ for remplacer the representations automorphes cuspidales with coefficients in $\mathbb{C}$ by celles with values in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$, the correspondence obtained depend, si $r$ is pair and $q$ a power impaire of $p$, of the racine carree $\iota\sqrt{q}$ of $q$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. Changer $\sqrt{q}$ en $-\sqrt{q}$ change the correspondence en sa composee with the twisting (see 0.3) by the character $n \mapsto (-1)^{n(r-1)}$ of $W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q) = \mathbb{Z}$.

\`A the correspondence utilisee by Lafforgue we preferons sa tordue by the character $n \mapsto \sqrt{q}^{\,n(r-1)}$ of $W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q)$. This correspondence rationalisee fournit a bijection between (A) and (B) independante of $\iota$.

\subsection*{0.3}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{0.3}

Tant for the objects (A) that for the objects (B) the twisting by a character $\chi: W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q) = \mathbb{Z} \to \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell^*$ is defined, and these torsions se correspondent.

the set of the characters $\chi$ of $W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q)$ is en bijection natural with the set of the classes of isomorphie of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil of rank a $\mathcal{L}_0$ on $\Spec(\mathbb{F}_q)$, and for the objects (A) the twisting is given by the tensor product with the inverse image, by $X_0 \to \Spec(\mathbb{F}_q)$, of a tel sheaf.

Let $v: A^* \to \mathbb{Z}$ the homomorphisme such that $|x|_k = q^{-v(x)}$. It se factorise by the group of the classes of ideles $K_0^* \setminus A^*$. In (B), si $\pi$ is a representation automorphe cuspidale of $GL(r,A)$, vue as contenue in the space of the functions locally constants on $GL(r,K_0) \setminus GL(r,A)$, the tordue $\pi\chi$ of $\pi$ by $\chi$ is the space of the functions $f(x)\chi(v(\det x))$ for $f$ in $\pi$.

We shall say parfois ``twisting by $b$'' for ``twisting by the character $\chi$ of $\mathbb{Z}$ such that $\chi(1)=b$''.

\subsection*{0.4}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{0.4}

The $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves forment a subcategory abelienne full of the abelian category of the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves of Weil. On $\Spec(\mathbb{F}_q)$, the class of isomorphie of a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil of rank a $\mathcal{L}_0$ is determinee by a character $\chi: W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q) = \mathbb{Z} \to \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell^*$, and for that $\mathcal{L}_0$ Let $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf it is necessary and sufficient that $\chi$ se prolonge en a character continu of $\Gal(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q) = \hat{\mathbb{Z}}$, i.e. that $\chi(1)$ Let unite $\ell$-adique. C'is this which oblige in 0.1(A) a utiliser the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves of Weil. Si one voulait in (A) se limiter to the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves, it faudrait in (B) se limiter to the representations automorphes cuspidales $\pi$ of which the character central $\omega_\pi$ se prolonge en a character continu of the complete profini of the group of the classes of ideles. This detruirait the character purement algebraic of (B).

The theorems suivants permettent of passer of the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves to the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves of Weil.

(a) Let $Z_0$ a variety connected normal of type finite on $\mathbb{F}_q$, and $\mathcal{F}_0$ a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil smooth irreducible of rank $r$ on $Z_0$. Then, $\mathcal{F}_0$ is a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf if and only if $\det(\mathcal{F}_0) := \bigwedge^r \mathcal{F}_0$ en is a ([De2] 1.3.14).

(b) Let $\mathcal{L}_0$ a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil smooth of rank a on $Z_0$. Definition: $\mathcal{L}_0$ is of ordre finite s'there exists $N > 0$ such that $\mathcal{L}_0^{\otimes N}$ let isomorphic to the sheaf constant $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. There exists toujours $N > 0$ such that $\mathcal{L}_0^{\otimes N}$ let the inverse image of a sheaf of Weil on $\Spec(\mathbb{F}_q)$ ([De2] 1.3.4 (i)). The group (for $\otimes$) of the classes of isomorphie of sheaves of Weil of rank a on $\Spec(\mathbb{F}_q)$ is divisible. All $\mathcal{L}_0$ is therefore the tensor product of a $\mathcal{L}_0'$, of ordre finite, and of the inverse image of a sheaf of Weil $\mathcal{L}_0''$ on $\Spec(\mathbb{F}_q)$. For that $\mathcal{L}_0$ Let $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf, it is necessary and sufficient that $\mathcal{L}_0''$ en Let.

(c) All $\mathcal{F}_0$ as en (a) is therefore deduces by twisting of a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf $\mathcal{F}_0'$ such that $\det(\mathcal{F}_0')$ let of ordre finite, and $\mathcal{F}_0$ is a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf if and only if the twisting is the tensor product with the inverse image of a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of rank a on $\Spec(\mathbb{F}_q)$.

In [L], Lafforgue states the correspondence between (A) and (B) en se limitant in (A) to the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves smooth irreductibles of which the determinant is of ordre finite, and en imposant in (B) a restriction corresponding to the representations automorphes. This which precede shows that it n'y perd rien.

\subsection*{0.5}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{0.5}

Notations. Let $\mathcal{F}_0$ a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil on $Z_0$ of type finite on $\mathbb{F}_q$, $x_0$ a point closed of $Z_0$ and $\deg(x_0) := [k(x_0):\mathbb{F}_q]$ son degree. The choix of $\bar{x}$ in $Z$ to the-dessus of $x_0$ defines a embedding of $k(x_0)$ in $k(\bar{x}) = \mathbb{F}$. The group of Weil $W(\mathbb{F}/k(x_0))$ is generated by the Frobenius geometric $F_{x_0}$. It is of indice $\deg(x_0)$ in $W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q)$, fixe $\bar{x}$ and agit on the fiber $\mathcal{F}_{\bar{x}}$ of $\mathcal{F}$ en the point geometric $\bar{x}$. In particular, $F_{x_0}$ agit on $\mathcal{F}_{\bar{x}}$. The factor local en $x_0$ of the function $L$ of $\mathcal{F}_0$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:0.5.1}
\det(1 - F_{x_0}t^{\deg(x_0)}, \mathcal{F}_{\bar{x}})^{-1}.
\end{equation}
It ne depend not of $\bar{x}$, only of $x_0$.

Let $n \geq 1$ and $x$ a $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$-point of $Z_0$: $x \in Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$. The point $x$ is a $\mathbb{F}_q$-morphism $\Spec(\mathbb{F}_{q^n}) \to Z_0$. Let $x_0$ the point closed of $Z_0$ which en is the image, and $\bar{x}$ the point geometric $\Spec(\mathbb{F}) \to \Spec(\mathbb{F}_{q^n}) \xrightarrow{x} Z_0$. One notera $F_x$ the generateur ``Frobenius geometric'' of $W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$. one has $W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_{q^n}) \subset W(\mathbb{F}/k(x_0))$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:0.5.2}
F_x = F_{x_0}^{n/\deg(x_0)}.
\end{equation}

One will say ``action of $F_x$ (resp.~$F_{x_0}$) on $\mathcal{F}_0$'' for ``action of $F_x$ (resp.~$F_{x_0}$) on $\mathcal{F}_{\bar{x}}$''. With this abus of langage, the factor local (\ref{eq:0.5.1}) s'ecrit
\[
\det(1 - F_{x_0}t^{\deg(x_0)}, \mathcal{F}_0)^{-1}.
\]

It we will be commode of considerer, plutot that these factors local, the traces $\tr(F_{x_0},\mathcal{F}_0)$ for $x$ in a $Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$. the identity between series formelles
\[
\log \det(1 - ft, V)^{-1} = \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{\tr(f^n,V)}{n} t^n,
\]
for $f$ a endomorphism of $V$, shows that these traces for $x$ to the-dessus of $x_0$ and the factor local en $x_0$ se determinent the a the other.

Lafforgue [L] VII 6 proves the theorem suivant, in lequel (ii) and (iii) resultent of the equivalence between (A) and (B) of 0.1.

\begin{theorem}[Lafforgue]\label{thm:0.6}
Let $X_0/\mathbb{F}_q$ as en 0.0, and $\mathcal{F}_0$ a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil smooth irreducible of rank $r$ on $X_0$, of which the determinant $\det(\mathcal{F}_0)$ is of ordre finite.

\emph{(i)} En all point closed $x_0$ of $X_0$, the values proper of $F_{x_0}$ agissant on $\mathcal{F}_0$ are of the nombres of Weil of weight $0$, i.e. are of the nombres algebraic of value absolute a en every place ne divisant not $p$. In particular, $\mathcal{F}_0$ is pur of weight $0$.

\emph{(ii)} There exists a finite extension $E \subset \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that for every point closed $x_0$ of $X_0$, the polynome $\det(1 - F_{x_0}t, \mathcal{F}_0)$ let with coefficients in $E$.

\emph{(iii)} For $E$ as en (ii), for every nombre prime $\ell' \neq p$ and for every embedding $\sigma$ of $E$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\ell'}$, there exists a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\ell'}$-sheaf of Weil smooth $\mathcal{F}_0'$ on $X_0$, such that en all point closed $x_0$ of $X_0$ one ait
\[
\det(1 - F_{x_0}t, \mathcal{F}_0') = \sigma \det(1 - F_{x_0}t, \mathcal{F}_0).
\]
\end{theorem}

the extension $E$ minimale is the field of definition of the representation automorphe $\pi$ corresponding a $\mathcal{F}_0$, vue to the choix as class of isomorphie of representation of $GL(r,A)$ or as under-space of the space of the functions on $GL(r,K_0) \setminus GL(r,A)$. It faut ici utiliser the correspondence rationalisee of 0.2.

\subsection*{0.7}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{0.7}

Let $Z_0$ a scheme connected normal of type finite on $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $\mathcal{F}_0$ a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil smooth irreducible on $Z_0$, of which the determinant is of ordre finite. Lafforgue [L] VII 7 shows, en se reduisant to the cas of the curves by a argument of sections planes, that the assertion (i) of the theorem \ref{thm:0.6} reste vraie for $\mathcal{F}_0$. Prendre garde that the reference a Hartshorne that Lafforgue given for the irreductibilite of the restriction of $\mathcal{F}_0$ a curve $X_0$ section plane of $Z_0$ n'is not adequate: Hartshorne assumed $Z_0$ projective. We expliquerons en 1.5--1.9 comment corriger the argument, en remplacant the reference a Hartshorne by a reference a Jouanolou [J].

\subsection*{0.8}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{0.8}

Let $\mathcal{F}_0$ and $Z_0$ as en 0.7. Utilisant a methode developpee by Wiesend [W] and the theorem of Lafforgue, Drinfeld [Dr] a shows, under the hypothese additionnelle that $Z_0$ is smooth, that si $\mathcal{F}_0$ satisfies the assertion (ii) of the theorem then $\mathcal{F}_0$ satisfies also (iii). Notre but is of montrer that all $\mathcal{F}_0$ as en 0.7 satisfies (ii).

\subsection*{0.9}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{0.9}

Passons en revue the sections of the present article. In the section 1, one considers the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves of Weil smooth semi-simples on $Z_0$ normal absolument irreducible of type finite on $\mathbb{F}_q$. One shows comment the decrire en terme of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves smooth on of the schemes $Z_0 \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q} \mathbb{F}_{q^a}$, of determinant of ordre finite, and of which the inverse image on $Z = Z_0 \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q} \mathbb{F}$ is irreducible. The decomposition (\ref{eq:1.4.1}) obtained traduit (0.3), joint a of the results bien connus on the relation between representations irreductibles of a group $G$ and of a extension of $\mathbb{Z}$ by $G$.

In the section 2, one considers a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil smooth $\mathcal{F}_0$ on a curve $X_0$ smooth and absolument irreducible on $\mathbb{F}_q$. For simplifier, one assumed $X_0$ affine. The ``complexite'' of $X_0$ will be mesuree by the integer $b_1(X_0) := \dim H_c^1(X, \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell)$. One assumed $\mathcal{F}_0$ algebraic, i.e. that the traces $\tr(F_{x_0},\mathcal{F}_0)$, for $x$ in a $X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, are of the nombres algebraic. of after \ref{thm:0.6} (ii) applique a of the tordus of the under-quotients irreductibles of $\mathcal{F}_0$, one sait that these traces engendrent a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. Notre but is of expliciter a integer $N$, dependant of a ``complexite'' of $(X_0,\mathcal{F}_0)$ such that $E$ let generated by the $\tr(F_{x_0},\mathcal{F}_0)$ for $x$ in a $X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ with $n \leq N$. Posons $\log_q^+(a) = \sup(0, \log_q(a))$. Si $\mathcal{F}$ is a ramification moderee, one obtains $N$ of the form
\begin{equation}\label{eq:0.9.1}
O(\log_q^+(b_1(X_0))) + O(1)
\end{equation}
or the constants implicites in $O$ dependent of the rank of $\mathcal{F}_0$. For $\mathcal{F}_0$ quelconque, it faut remplacer $b_1(X_0)$ by $b_1(X_0) + \sum_s \alpha_s(\mathcal{F})$, or $\alpha_s(\mathcal{F})$ mesure the sauvagerie of the ramification of $\mathcal{F}$ en $s \in S$.

A other facon of mesurer the sauvagerie of $\mathcal{F}$, beaucoup less economique but which will be commode in the section 3, is en terme of a etale cover connected $X'$ of $X$ on lequel the inverse image of $\mathcal{F}$ is a ramification moderee. One obtiendra a other $N$, of the form
\begin{equation}\label{eq:0.9.2}
O(\log_q^+(b_1(X'))) + O(1).
\end{equation}
Ici also, the constants implicites in $O$ dependent of the rank of $\mathcal{F}_0$.

The proofs font a usage essential of \ref{thm:0.6} (iii), for ramener the probleme pose to the suivant. For $\mathcal{F}_0$ and $\mathcal{G}_0$ of the sheaves of Weil smooth semi-simples on $X_0$, trouver $N$ such that si $\tr(F_{x_0},\mathcal{F}_0) = \tr(F_{x_0},\mathcal{G}_0)$ for every $x$ in a $X(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ with $n \leq N$, then $\mathcal{F}_0$ and $\mathcal{G}_0$ are isomorphes.

\subsection*{0.10}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{0.10}

The theorem principal is proves in the section 3. After some devissages, one is amene a traiter the cas or $\mathcal{F}_0$ is a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf smooth on a scheme $Z_0$ which is smooth and absolument irreducible on $\mathbb{F}_q$, and or $\mathcal{F}_0$ is algebraic (algebricite of the traces of the Frobenius). It s'agit of montrer that the extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ generated by the traces of the Frobenius is a finite extension. One the fait en montrant that there exists a integer $N$ such that for every integer $n > N$ and all point $x \in Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, the trace $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ is contenue in the extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ generated by the $\tr(F_{x'_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ with $x'$ in a $Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n'}})$ and $n' < n$. For the prouver, one fait passer by $x$ a curve $X_0$ such that $(X_0, \mathcal{F}_0|_{X_0})$ ne let not trop complex, and one applique a this curve the results of the section 2. More precisely, one constructs a curve affine smooth $X_0$, a point $\tilde{x} \in X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ and a $\mathbb{F}_q$-morphism $\phi: X_0 \to Z_0$ which envoie $\tilde{x}$ on $x$. The construction ne garantit not that the curve $X_0$ let connected. Remplacons-the by sa composante connected $X_1$ such that $\tilde{x} \in X_1(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$. The curve $X_1$ pourrait ne not be absolument irreducible on $\mathbb{F}_q$, but one dispose of a borne $D$ (ne dependant that of $Z_0$) such that $X_1$ let absolument irreducible on a $\mathbb{F}_{q^d}$ with $d \leq D$. C'is a $X_1/\mathbb{F}_{q^d}$ that one appliquera the results of the section 2. For simplifier the expose of the strategie, we pretendons ici (a tort) $X_0$ absolument irreducible on $\mathbb{F}_q$.

Choisissons a etale cover connected $Z'$ of $Z$ on lequel $\mathcal{F}$ devienne a ramification moderee. This is a enorme gaspillage but n'is fait that a seule fois. Let $X'$ a composante connected of the inverse image of $Z'$ on $X$. The complexite of $(X_1, \phi^* \mathcal{F}_0)$ will be mesuree by $b_1(X')$. We the controlerons by the theorem of Katz [K]. As it ne s'agit ici that of curves, one pourrait plutot utiliser Bombieri [B], on lequel se base Katz, and estimer the nombre of composantes connected by the product of the degrees of equations of $X'$, but this ne serait that refaire in a cas simple the argument of Katz. One obtains a borne for the complexite which is polynomiale en $n$. Of the that $n$ is sufficiently grand, the integer $N$ of (\ref{eq:0.9.2}) satisfies $N < n$ and $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0) = \tr(F_{\tilde{x}}, \phi^* \mathcal{F}_0)$ is in the extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ generated by the $\tr(F_{x'_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ for $x' \in X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n'}})$ and $n' \leq N < n$.

Je remercie H.~Esnault of a lecture attentive of the texte and of ses suggestions which m'have permis, je the espere, of the rendre more lisible.

\section{Irreductibilite and extensions of the field of base}

\subsection{1.1}

Let $Z_0$ a scheme normal absolument irreducible of type finite on $\mathbb{F}_q$, $Z := Z_0 \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q} \mathbb{F}$ and $x$ a point geometric of $Z$. It defines a point geometric, again note $x$, of $Z_0$. The fundamental group of $Z_0$ is a extension
\[
1 \to \pi_1(Z,x) \to \pi_1(Z_0,x) \to \Gal(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q) \to 1
\]
Prenant the fiber product with $W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q) = \mathbb{Z} \subset \Gal(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q) = \hat{\mathbb{Z}}$, one obtains the group of Weil $W(Z_0,x)$:
\[
1 \to \pi_1(Z,x) \to W(Z_0,x) \to \mathbb{Z} \to 1.
\]
The functor ``fiber en $x$'' is a equivalence of the category of the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves of Weil smooth on $Z_0$ with celle of the representations lineaires continues of $W(Z_0,x)$ on a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-space vector of dimension finite.

\subsection{1.2}

Si $V$ is a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-representation irreducible of $W(Z_0,x)$, sa restriction a $\pi_1(Z,x)$ is sum of representations irreductibles not isomorphes of $\pi_1(Z,x)$, permutees between they transitivement by $W(Z_0,x)/\pi_1(Z_0,x) = \mathbb{Z}$.

Let $n$ the nombre of sommands, and $Z_1 := Z_0 \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q} \mathbb{F}_{q^n}$; $W(Z_1,x)$ is the inverse image in $W(Z_0,x)$ of $n\mathbb{Z}$. Si $S$ is the a of the sommands irreductibles of the restriction of $V$ a $\pi_1(Z,x)$, $S$ is a representation of $W(Z_1,x)$ and $V$ is the induite $\Ind_{W(Z_1,x)}^{W(Z_0,x)}(S)$.

Si $\mathcal{V}$ (resp.~$\mathcal{S}$) is the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil corresponding a $V$ (resp.~$S$), $\mathcal{V}$ is the direct image, by $Z_1 \to Z_0$, of $\mathcal{S}$.

\subsection{1.3}

Let maintenant $V$ a representation semisimple of $W(Z_0,x)$. The quotient $\mathbb{Z}$ of $W(Z_0,x)$ permute the classes of isomorphie of constituants simples of the restriction of $V$ a $\pi_1(Z,x)$. Let $A$ the set of the orbites, in each orbite $a$ choisissons a representant $S'_a$, and let $n(a)$ the nombre of elements of the orbite. Si $Z_a = Z_0 \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q} \mathbb{F}_{q^{n(a)}}$, the representation $S'_a$ se prolonge en a representation $S_a$ of $W(Z_a,x)$, and $S_a$ is unique a twisting pres by a character of the quotient $\mathbb{Z}$ of $W(Z_a,x)$. We choisirons the twisting for that the character $\det(S_a)$ of $W(Z_a,x)$ let of ordre finite.

Appliquons 1.2 to the constituants irreductibles of $V$, and regroupons the occurrences of $S_a$. One obtains a decomposition
\begin{equation}\label{eq:1.3.1}
V = \bigoplus_a \Ind_{W(Z_a,x)}^{W(Z_0,x)}(S_a \otimes W_a)
\end{equation}
for $W_a$ a representation of $W(Z_a,x)$ trivial on $\pi_1(Z,x)$. This description of $V$ is unique, a that pres that one can

(a) tordre $S_a$ by a character of ordre finite of $\mathbb{Z} = W(Z_a,x)/\pi_1(Z,x)$, and $W_a$ by the character inverse;

(b) remplacer $S_a$ by son conjugue $S_a(i)$ by a element $i$ of $W(Z_0,x)/W(Z_a,x) = \mathbb{Z}/n(a)$.

\subsection{1.4}

Passons of the langage of the representations of groups a celui of the sheaves: $S_a$ (resp.~$S_a(i)$) correspond a $\mathcal{S}_{a,1}$ (resp.~$\mathcal{S}_{a,1}^{(i)}$) on $Z_a$, $W_a$ a $\mathcal{W}_a$ on $\Spec(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n(a)}})$ and, si $p_a$ is the projection of $Z_a$ on $Z_0$, and $pr_a$ celle of $Z_a$ on $\Spec(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n(a)}})$, (\ref{eq:1.3.1}) devient a decomposition of the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil $\mathcal{V}$ corresponding a $V$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:1.4.1}
\mathcal{V} = \bigoplus_{a \in A} p_a^*(\mathcal{S}_{a,1} \otimes pr_a^* \mathcal{W}_a).
\end{equation}
In this decomposition, the $\det(\mathcal{S}_a)$ are of ordre finite, and the images inverses $\mathcal{S}_a^{(i)}$ on $Z$ of the $\mathcal{S}_{a,1}^{(i)}$ ($a \in A$, $i \in \mathbb{Z}/n(a)$) are of the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves irreductibles not isomorphes.

\subsection{1.5}

Let $\mathcal{F}_0$ smooth irreducible of determinant of ordre finite on $Z_0$ as en 1.1. of after 1.2, the inverse image $\mathcal{F}$ of $\mathcal{F}_0$ on $Z := Z_0 \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q} \mathbb{F}$ is direct sum of sheaves smooth irreductibles $\mathcal{S}^{(i)}$ not isomorphes, permutes transitivement by $\mathbb{Z} = W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_q)$. One denotes $n$ the nombre of the $\mathcal{S}^{(i)}$. In the fin of this section, we donnons a proof of the states [L] VII 7 suivant of Lafforgue (cf 0.7)

\begin{theorem}[Lafforgue]\label{thm:1.6}
En all point closed $x_0$ of $Z_0$, the values proper of $F_{x_0}$ agissant on $\mathcal{F}_0$ are of the nombres of Weil of weight $0$.

Si $U_0$ is a open not vide of $Z_0$, the restriction of $\mathcal{F}_0$ a $U_0$ is again irreducible. Recouvrant $Z_0$ by of the ouverts affine, one se ramene a supposer, and one supposera, that $Z_0$ is affine.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:1.7}
There exists a etale cover connected galoisien $Z'$ of $Z_0$ such that si the inverse image $Y'$ of $Z'$ by a morphism $f: Y \to Z_0$ is connected, then $\mathcal{F}_0$ and $f^* \mathcal{F}_0$ have same monodromy.

Fixons a point base $a$ of $Y$, and notons again $a$ son image in $Z_0$. One dispose of a morphism

\]
and the conclusion ``same monodromy'' signifie that $\pi_1(Y,a)$ s'envoie on the image of $\pi_1(X,a)$ in $GL(\mathcal{F}_a)$. It implique that the $f^* \mathcal{S}^{(i)}$ restent smooth irreductibles not isomorphes.

\noindent\textit{Proof of \ref{lem:1.7}.} The group of monodromy $M$, image of $\pi_1(X,a)$ in $GL(\mathcal{F}_a)$, is a under-group closed of a group $GL(n, \mathcal{O}_\lambda)$, therefore is a Lie group $\ell$-adique compact. It admet therefore a pro-$\ell$ under-group invariant open $H$, and the intersection $H'$ of the noyaux of the homomorphismes $H \to \mathbb{Z}/\ell$ is again a under-group invariant open. One prend for $Z'$ the covering corresponding a $H'$. Supposons $Y'$ connected. This equivaut a this that $\pi_1(Y,a)$ s'envoie on $M/H'$. Puisque all under-group closed of $H$ which s'envoie on $H/H'$ co\"ncide with $H$, $\pi_1(Y,a)$ s'envoie on $M$.

\subsection{1.8}

Choisissons a embedding closed of $Z_0$ in a affine space type $\mathbb{A}_0^{k}$ on $\mathbb{F}_q$ and $Z'$ as en \ref{lem:1.7}. Let $G_0$ the $\mathbb{F}_q$-scheme which parametrise the under-spaces lineaires affine of codimension $\dim(Z_0)-1$ in $\mathbb{A}_0^{k}$. The nombre of $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-points of $U_0$ is, for $m \to \infty$, of the form $q^{m\dim(U)}(1+O(q^{-m/2}))$ (Lang-Weil or the formule of the traces more the Weil conjecture). Appliquons-lui \ref{thm:0.6}(i): quelque let the point closed $y_0$ of $Y_0 \subset Z_0$, the values proper of $F_{y_0}$ agissant on $\mathcal{F}_0$ are of the nombres of Weil of weight $0$. One conclut by the

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:1.9}
Let $\mathcal{F}_0$ a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil smooth on a scheme connected $X_0$ on $\mathbb{F}_q$. The conditions suivantes are equivalentes:

\emph{(i)} there exists a point closed $x_0$ of $X_0$ such that the values proper of $F_{x_0}$ agissant on $\mathcal{F}_0$ let of the nombres of Weil of weight $0$;

\emph{(ii)} same assertion en all the points fermes of $X_0$.
\end{proposition}

\noindent\textit{Proof (for $X_0$ a curve smooth and connected).} Assume that $\mathcal{F}_0$ satisfies (i). All under-quotient irreducible $\mathcal{F}'_0$ satisfies again (i), and it is enough to verify (ii) for each $\mathcal{F}'_0$. Testant en $x_0$, one sees that the twisting is by a nombre of Weil of weight $0$, and the validite of (ii) is invariante by a telle twisting.

\medskip
\noindent\textit{Proof (cas general).} For every the point closed $x'_0$ of $X_0$, there exists a sequence of curves smooth and connected $Y_j$ and of morphisms $f_j: Y_j \to X_0$ ($1 \leq j \leq N$) such that $x_0$ let in the image of $Y_1$, $x'_0$ in celle of $Y_N$, and that the intersection of the images of $Y_j$ and $Y_{j+1}$ ($1 \leq j < N$) let not vide. Si (i) is satisfies en $x_0$, the premiere part of the proof shows that (ii) is satisfies for the inverse image of $\mathcal{F}_0$ on $Y_1$, therefore that (i) is satisfies en all point closed of $X_0$ in the image of $Y_1$. Similarly, si (i) is satisfies en the points fermes in $f_j(Y_j)$, therefore en to the less a point closed of $f_{j+1}(Y_{j+1})$, (i) is satisfies en the points fermes in $f_{j+1}(Y_{j+1})$, and one atteint finalement $x'_0$.


\section{The cas of the curves: versions quantitatives}

\subsection{2.1}

Let $X$ a curve smooth and connected over a field algebriquement clos of caracteristique $p$, $\bar{X}$ the completee projective and smooth of $X$ and $S$ the set of the points a the infini: $X = \bar{X} - S$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf smooth of rank $r$ on $X$. Posons
\[
\chi_c(X, \mathcal{F}) := \sum_i (-1)^i \dim H_c^i(X, \mathcal{F}).
\]
This caracteristique of Euler-Poincare is given by the formule of Grothendieck-Ogg-Shafarevich
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.1.1}
\chi_c(X, \mathcal{F}) = r\chi_c(X) - \sum_{s \in S} \Sw_s(\mathcal{F}).
\end{equation}
Si the curve $\bar{X}$ is of genre $g$, one has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.1.2}
\chi_c(X) = 2 - 2g - |S|.
\end{equation}
The terme $\Sw_s(\mathcal{F})$ is the conducteur of Swan of $\mathcal{F}$ en $s$.

Let $K_s$ the field of the fractions of the henselise of $X$ en $s$. The reader which the prefere can remplacer ``henselise'' by ``complete''. That ne change not $\Gal(\bar{K}_s/K_s)$, for $\bar{K}_s$ a algebraic closure of $K_s$. The $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves on $\Spec(K_s)$ s'identifient to the representations continues $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-lineaires $V$ of $\Gal(\bar{K}_s/K_s)$. The conducteur $\Sw_s(\mathcal{F})$ is the conducteur of Swan $\Sw(V)$ of the representation lineaire $V$ of $\Gal(\bar{K}_s/K_s)$ corresponding a the inverse image of $\mathcal{F}$ on $\Spec(K_s)$.

The conducteur $\Sw(V)$ is additif en $V$ (for the sequences exact courtes). Notons $\Gal(\bar{K}_s/K_s)^\beta$ the under-groups of ramification of $\Gal(\bar{K}_s/K_s)$, en numerotation superieure. Definissons $\alpha(V)$ as being the borne inferieure of the $\beta > 0$ such that $\Gal(\bar{K}_s/K_s)^\beta$ agisse trivialement on $V$. Si the representation $V$ is irreducible, one has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.1.3}
\Sw(V) = \dim(V) \cdot \alpha(V) \quad \text{(V irr\'eductible)}
\end{equation}
(a consequence of Serre [S] 19.1 and of the definition of the functions of Herbrand reliant the numerotation inferieure a the numerotation superieure). Si $V$ provient of $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$, one posera $\alpha_s(\mathcal{F}) := \alpha(V)$.

It follows of (\ref{eq:2.1.3}) by additivite that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.1.4}
\Sw(V) \leq \dim(V) \cdot \alpha(V).
\end{equation}

Let $P$ the pro-$p$-under-group of Sylow of $\Gal(\bar{K}_s/K_s)$. Puisque $V$ is $\ell$-adique, it agit on $V$ a travers a quotient finite $\bar{P}$.

Tant $\Sw(V)$ that $\alpha(V)$ s'annulent if and only if $V$ is moderee, i.e. si $P$ agit trivialement. Otherwise, $\alpha(V)$ is the more grand nombre (rational) such that $\bar{P}^{\alpha(V)}$ let not trivial. the importance for we of the invariant $\alpha(V)$ provient of the observation that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.1.5}
\alpha(V \otimes W) \leq \sup(\alpha(V), \alpha(W)).
\end{equation}

The duality of Poincare met en duality parfaite $H_c^2(X, \mathcal{F})$ and $H^0(X, \mathcal{F}^\vee(1))$. In particular, $H_c^2(X, \mathcal{F})$ is of rank to the more $r$ and of rank $r$ si $\mathcal{F}$ is constant. Si the curve $X$ is affine, one has $H_c^0(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$, and (\ref{eq:2.1.1}), (\ref{eq:2.1.4}) donnent
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.1.6}
\dim H_c^1(X, \mathcal{F}) \leq r(b_1(X) + \sum_s \alpha_s(\mathcal{F})) \quad (X \text{ affine}),
\end{equation}
or one has pose
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.1.7}
b_1(X) = \dim H_c^1(X, \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell) = 2g + |S| - 1 \quad (X \text{ affine}).
\end{equation}

\subsection{2.2}

Let $X = \bar{X} - S$ a curve on $\mathbb{F}_q$ as en 0.0, and $\mathcal{F}_0$ a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil smooth of rank $r$ on $X_0$. One assumed $\mathcal{F}_0$ algebraic (0.9). One ne assumed not $\mathcal{F}_0$ irreducible. Let $E$ a extension galoisienne of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ contenant the $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ for $x$ in a quelconque $X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, $n \geq 1$. of after 0.6, for every $\sigma \in \Gal(E/\mathbb{Q})$, there exists a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil smooth semisimple $\sigma(\mathcal{F}_0)$ such that for every $x$ in a $X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, one ait
\[
\tr(F_{x_0}, \sigma(\mathcal{F}_0)) = \sigma(\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)).
\]
One notera $\sigma(\mathcal{F})$ the inverse image of $\sigma(\mathcal{F}_0)$ on $X$. This notation is raisonnable, car $\sigma(\mathcal{F})$, which is defined a isomorphism pres, ne depend that of $\mathcal{F}$ (resulte of \ref{eq:1.4.1} and of a compatibility between ``$\sigma$'' and twisting). For each $s \in S$, one has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.2.1}
\Sw_s(\sigma \mathcal{F}) = \Sw_s(\mathcal{F}), \quad \alpha_s(\sigma \mathcal{F}) = \alpha_s(\mathcal{F}).
\end{equation}
Esquisse of proof: one can supposer $\mathcal{F}_0$ irreducible. Si $\mathcal{F}_0$ correspond a representation automorphe $\pi$ (by the correspondence rationalisee), $\pi$ is defined on $E$ and $\sigma \mathcal{F}_0$ correspond a $\sigma \pi$. En each $s \in S$, $\mathcal{F}_0$ defines a representation of the group of Weil local. By the correspondence local, sa Frobenius-semi-simplifiee ([De1] 8.6) correspond a the composante local $\pi_s$ of $\pi$. Noter that the classes of isomorphie of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-representations lineaires continues $F$-semi-simples of the group of Weil local are en correspondence bijective with the classes of isomorphie of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-representations lineaires $F$-semisimple (loc.~cit.) of the group of Weil-Deligne. These dernieres are of the objects purement algebraic. Si $\pi_s$ is defined on $E$, the representation corresponding the will be also, and conjuguer by $\sigma$ is compatible a the correspondence (rationalisee). In particular, $\mathcal{F}_0$ and $\sigma(\mathcal{F}_0)$ donnent lieu a of the representations of the group of inertie sauvage en $s$ ayant the same kernel, and one se reduit a (\ref{eq:2.1.3}).

For notre result principal, the lemma more elementaire suivant suffit.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:2.3}
Si $\mathcal{F}_0$ is moderement ramifie, $\sigma(\mathcal{F}_0)$ the is also.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textit{Proof.} the image by $\sigma$ of the function $L$ of $\mathcal{F}_0$:
\[
L(X_0, \mathcal{F}_0, t) = \prod_{x \in X_0} \det(1 - F_{x_0} t^{\deg(x_0)}, \mathcal{F}_0)^{-1} \in \mathbb{Q}(t)
\]
is the function $L$ of $\sigma(\mathcal{F}_0)$. This function $L$ is a function rational, and of after the interpretation cohomologique of Grothendieck of the functions $L$ the ordre of son pole en $t = \infty$ is $-\chi_c(\mathcal{F})$. one has therefore $\chi_c(\mathcal{F}) = \chi_c(\sigma \mathcal{F})$. Puisque $\mathcal{F}_0$ is a ramification moderee, the $\Sw_s(\mathcal{F})$ are nuls. Comparaissant (\ref{eq:2.1.1}) for $\mathcal{F}$ and $\sigma \mathcal{F}$, one sees that the sum of the $\Sw_s(\sigma \mathcal{F})$, and therefore chacun of eux, is zero, i.e. that $\sigma(\mathcal{F}_0)$ is a ramification moderee.

\subsection{2.4}

Supposons $X$ affine, and let $\mathcal{F}_0$, $\mathcal{G}_0$ deux sheaves of Weil smooth semi-simples of rank $r$ on $X_0$. Notons $\log_q^+$ the function $\sup(0, \log_q)$ and $[\ ]$ the function ``part integer''. Posons
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.4.1}
\alpha_s(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}) := \alpha_s(\mathcal{F} \oplus \mathcal{G}) = \sup(\alpha_s(\mathcal{F}), \alpha_s(\mathcal{G}))
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.4.2}
N_0 = 2\log_q^+\left(2r^2 \cdot b_1(X) + \sum_{s \in S} \alpha_s(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})\right)
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.4.3}
N = [N_0] + 2r.
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:2.5}
Si for every integer $n \leq N$ and all $x \in X(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ one has
\[
\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0) = \tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{G}_0),
\]
then $\mathcal{F}_0$ is isomorphic a $\mathcal{G}_0$.
\end{proposition}

\noindent\textit{Proof.} Appliquons (\ref{eq:1.3.1}) (\ref{eq:1.4.1}) a $\mathcal{F}_0 \oplus \mathcal{G}_0$. One obtains of the decompositions (\ref{eq:1.4.1})
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.5.1}
\mathcal{F}_0 = \bigoplus_{a \in A} p_a^*(\mathcal{S}_{a,1} \otimes pr_a^* \mathcal{W}_a), \quad \mathcal{G}_0 = \bigoplus_{a \in A} p_a^*(\mathcal{S}_{a,1} \otimes pr_a^* \mathcal{W}'_a).
\end{equation}
In (\ref{eq:2.5.1}), a each $a \in A$ is attached a integer $n(a) \geq 1$, $\mathcal{S}_{a,1}$ is a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil smooth on $X_a := X_0 \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q} \mathbb{F}_{q^{n(a)}}$, $\mathcal{W}_a$ and $\mathcal{W}'_a$ are of the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves of Weil on $\Spec(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n(a)}})$, and $p_a$ and $pr_a$ are the projections of $X_a$ on $X_0$ and on $\Spec(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n(a)}})$. Notons $\mathcal{S}_{a,1}^{(i)}$, the image of $\mathcal{S}_{a,1}$, by the power $i$eme of the Frobenius $F \in \Gal(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n(a)}}/\mathbb{F}_q)$, and omettons the indice $1$ for indiquer the inverse image of $X_a$ a $X$. of after (1.4), the $\mathcal{S}_{a,1}$, $\mathcal{W}_a$ and $\mathcal{W}'_a$ in (\ref{eq:2.5.1}) satisfy

(i) $\det(\mathcal{S}_{a,1})$ is of ordre finite;

(ii) the $\mathcal{S}_{a,1}^{(i)}$ ($a \in A$, $i \in \mathbb{Z}/n(a)$) are of the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves smooth irreductibles on $X$, deux a deux not isomorphes;

(iii) For each $a$, $\mathcal{W}_a$ or $\mathcal{W}'_a$ is not zero.

Puisque $\mathcal{S}_a^{(i)}$ is a direct factor of $\mathcal{F}$ or of $\mathcal{G}$, one has en all point $s \in S$
\[
\alpha_s(\mathcal{S}_a^{(i)}) \leq \sup(\alpha_s(\mathcal{F}), \alpha_s(\mathcal{G})).
\]
Notons $A(n)$ the set of the $a$ in $A$ such that $n(a) | n$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:2.6}
Si $n > N_0$ (\ref{eq:2.4.2}), the functions on $X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$
\[
t_{a,i}: x \mapsto \tr(F_x, \mathcal{S}_{a,1}^{(i)}) \quad (a \in A(n), i \in \mathbb{Z}/n(a))
\]
are lineairement independantes.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textit{Proof.} The functions $t_{a,i}$ are with values in a number field $E \subset \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. Plongeons $E$ in $\mathbb{C}$ for the traiter as of the functions a values complexes. the idee of the proof is of montrer that they are presque orthogonales, in $L^2(X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n}))$.

of after \ref{thm:0.6}(i), $\mathcal{S}_{a,1}^{(i)}$ is pur of weight $0$. The function complex conjuguee of $t_{a,i}$ is therefore $x \mapsto \tr(F_x, \mathcal{S}_{a,1}^{\vee(i)})$, and the product scalaire $\langle t_{a,i}, t_{b,j} \rangle = \sum_x t_{a,i}(x) \overline{t_{b,j}(x)}$ is
\[
\langle t_{a,i}, t_{b,j} \rangle = \sum_x \tr(F_x, \Hom(\mathcal{S}_{a,1}^{(i)}, \mathcal{S}_{b,1}^{(j)})).
\]
By the formule of the traces, this sum is the trace of the Frobenius $F \in W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.6.1}
\langle t_{a,i}, t_{b,j} \rangle = \sum_k (-1)^k \tr(F, H_c^k(X, \Hom(\mathcal{S}_a^{(i)}, \mathcal{S}_b^{(j)}))).
\end{equation}
Puisque $X$ is affine, $H_c^0$ is zero. The terme ``dominant'' is given by $H_c^2$: it vaut $q^n$ si $(a,i) = (b,j)$ and is zero otherwise. The presque orthogonalite promise vient of this that the terme $k=1$ is en $O(q^{n/2})$ for $n$ grand. More precisely, puisque $\Hom(\mathcal{S}_a^{(i)}, \mathcal{S}_b^{(j)})$ is pur of weight $0$, the values proper of $F$ on son $H_c^1$ are of value absolute $q^{n/2}$ or $1$, and the terme $k=1$ is borne en value absolute by $q^{n/2} \cdot \dim \mathcal{S}_a^{(i)} \cdot \dim \mathcal{S}_b^{(j)} \cdot (b_1(X) + \sum_s \alpha_s(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}))$.

Assume that there exists a relation of dependance lineaire $\sum \lambda_{b,j} t_{b,j} = 0$. Let $a,i$ such that $|\lambda_{a,i}|$ let maximal parmi the $|\lambda_{b,j}|$. Divisant by $\lambda_{a,i}$, one can supposer that $\lambda_{a,i} = 1$ and that $|\lambda_{b,j}| \leq 1$ for $b \in A(n)$ and $j \in \mathbb{Z}/n(b)$. one has then
\[
0 = \langle \sum \lambda_{b,j} t_{b,j}, t_{a,i} \rangle = q^n + \text{reste}
\]
or the value absolute of the reste is majoree by
\[
\sum_{b,j} |\lambda_{b,j}| \cdot |\tr(F, H_c^1(X, \Hom(\mathcal{S}_a^{(i)}, \mathcal{S}_b^{(j)})))| \leq q^{n/2} \cdot 2r^2 \cdot (b_1(X) + \sum_s \alpha_s(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})).
\]
the hypothese on $n$ assure that $|\text{reste}| < q^n$: contradiction.

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:2.7}
Notons $F$ the Frobenius of $W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$. Si $n > N_0$ and that $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0) = \tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{G}_0)$ for $x \in X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, then
\[
\tr(F, \mathcal{W}_a) = \tr(F, \mathcal{W}'_a)
\]
for each $a \in A(n)$.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textit{Proof.} The decompositions (\ref{eq:2.5.1}) fournissent the identity between functions traces
\[
\sum_i \tr(F, \mathcal{W}_a) = \sum_i \tr(F, \mathcal{W}'_a)
\]
and one applique \ref{lem:2.6}.

\subsection{2.8}

Fin of the proof of \ref{prop:2.5}. It faut montrer that for each $a$, and for $F$ the Frobenius geometric generateur of $W(\mathbb{F}/\mathbb{F}_{q^{n(a)}})$, $F$ a same multi-set of values proper on $\mathcal{W}_a$ and $\mathcal{W}'_a$. of after \ref{cor:2.7}, si $n$ is divisible by $n(a)$ and that $[N_0]+1 \leq n \leq N = [N_0]+2r$, one has
\[
\tr(F^{n/n(a)}, \mathcal{W}_a) = \tr(F^{n/n(a)}, \mathcal{W}'_a).
\]
There is to the less $[2r/a]$ telles values of $n$, $\mathcal{W}_a$ and $\mathcal{W}'_a$ are of dimension to the more $[r/a]$ and it reste a appliquer the lemma suivant

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:2.9}
Let $\alpha_i$ $k$ nombres not nuls distincts. Si the $\lambda_i$ satisfy, for $m$ suitable,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.9.1}
\sum_i \lambda_i \alpha_i^r = 0 \quad \text{pour} \quad m \leq r < m+k,
\end{equation}
the $\lambda_i$ are all nuls.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textit{Proof.} (\ref{eq:2.9.1}) can se recrire
\[
\sum_i (\lambda_i \alpha_i^m) \cdot \alpha_i^s = 0 \quad \text{pour} \quad 0 \leq s < k
\]
and the determinant of Vandermonde $\det(\alpha_i^s)$ is not zero.

\subsection{2.10}

In the proposition which suit, $X_0$ is assumed affine, and $\mathcal{F}_0$ is a sheaf of Weil smooth of rank $r$ on $X_0$. One assumed that $\mathcal{F}_0$ is algebraic to the sens of 0.9. Posons
\[
N_0 = 2\log_q^+\left(2r^2 \cdot b_1(X) + \sum_s \alpha_s(\mathcal{F})\right), \quad N = [N_0] + 2r.
\]
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:2.10}
Let $E_0$ the extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ generated by the $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ for $x$ in a $X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ with $n \leq N$. Then, for every $n$ and all $x \in X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ is in $E_0$.
\end{proposition}

\noindent\textit{Proof.} Semi-simplifiant $\mathcal{F}_0$, one se ramene a supposer $\mathcal{F}_0$ semisimple. Let $E$ as en 2.2 a extension galoisienne sufficiently grande of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. It we faut montrer that for $\sigma \in \Gal(E/E_0)$, the $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ are fixes by $\sigma$. This equivaut a
\begin{equation}\label{eq:2.10.1}
\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0) = \tr(F_{x_0}, \sigma(\mathcal{F}_0)).
\end{equation}
By hypothese, (\ref{eq:2.10.1}) is vraie si $x$ is in a $X(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ with $n \leq N$. of after \ref{prop:2.5} and the fait that $\alpha_s(\mathcal{F}_0) = \alpha_s(\sigma(\mathcal{F}_0))$, $\mathcal{F}_0$ is isomorphic a $\sigma(\mathcal{F}_0)$. the assertion en resulte.

\subsection{2.11}

Variantes. Gardons the hypotheses and notations of \ref{prop:2.5}. Let $q: X' \to X$ a etale cover connected of $X$ on lequel the images inverses of $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ Let ramification moderee. For every $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf $\mathcal{H}$ on $X$, of which the inverse image on $X'$ is a ramification moderee, the morphism
\[
q^*: H_c^*(X, \mathcal{H}) \to H_c^*(X', q^*\mathcal{H})
\]
is injective, car son compose with $\tr_q$ is the multiplication by the degree of the covering. one has therefore
\[
\dim H_c^1(X, \mathcal{H}) \leq \dim H_c^1(X', \mathcal{H}) \leq \rang(\mathcal{H}) \cdot b_1(X').
\]
Si one repete the arguments prouvant \ref{prop:2.5} en utilisant this estimation plutot that (\ref{eq:2.1.6}), one obtains:

\begin{variante}\label{var:2.12}
Posons $N'_0 := 2\log_q^+(2r^2 b_1(X'))$ and $N' := [N'_0]+2r$. Si for every integer $n \leq N'$ and all $x \in X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, one has
\[
\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0) = \tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{G}_0),
\]
then $\mathcal{F}_0$ is isomorphic a $\mathcal{G}_0$.
\end{variante}

Similarly si $\mathcal{F}_0$ is as en \ref{prop:2.10}, and that son inverse image by $q: X' \to X$ is a ramification moderee, $\sigma(\mathcal{F}_0)$ a the same property: after a finite extension of the field of base $\mathbb{F}_q$, one can supposer that $q: X' \to X$ provient of $q_0: X'_0 \to X_0$ and one applique \ref{lem:2.3}. Repetant similarly the arguments which prouvent \ref{prop:2.10}, one obtains the

\begin{variante}\label{var:2.13}
Let $E'_0$ the extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ generated by the $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ for $x$ in a $X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ with $n \leq N'$, $N'$ being as en \ref{var:2.12}. Then, for every $n$ and all $x \in X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ is in $E'_0$.
\end{variante}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:2.14}
the hypothese that $\mathcal{F}_0$ is algebraic assure that $E'_0$ is a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. It n'is not requise for prouver \ref{var:2.13}. Si $E_0 \subset E$ are of the extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$, si $\Sigma$ is the set of the $\sigma: E \to \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ which prolongent the inclusion of $E_0$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$, then
\[
E_0 = \{e \in E \mid \sigma(e) = e \text{ pour tout } \sigma \in \Sigma\},
\]
and this observation can se substituer a the argument galoisien.
\end{remark}

\section{The theorem principal}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:3.1}
Let $Z_0$ a scheme of type finite on $\mathbb{F}_q$. Si $\mathcal{F}_0$ is a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf of Weil algebraic (0.9) on $Z_0$, there exists a finite extension $E \subset \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that for every $n$ and all $x \in Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ let in $E$.
\end{theorem}

That these traces let all in $E$ revient a this that en all point closed $x_0$ of $Z_0$ the factor local of the function $L$ of $\mathcal{F}_0$ let with coefficients in $E$ (see 0.5).

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:3.2}
The theorem \ref{thm:3.1} is implique by son cas particulier or one assumed that

\emph{(i)} $Z_0$ is affine, smooth, irreducible, and is equipped with a morphism étale $\phi: Z_0 \to \mathbb{A}_0^{k}$ toward a affine space on $\mathbb{F}_q$;

\emph{(ii)} $\mathcal{F}_0$ is smooth, irreducible and $\det(\mathcal{F}_0)$ is of ordre finite.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textit{Proof.} The scheme $Z_0$ of \ref{thm:3.1} admet a partition en parties locally fermees irreductibles $\mathcal{F}_i$ verifiant (i) and such that $\mathcal{F}_0|_{\mathcal{F}_i}$ let smooth. It is enough to traiter separement each $(\mathcal{F}_i, \mathcal{F}_0|_{\mathcal{F}_i})$. One can ensuite traiter separement each under-quotient irreducible of $\mathcal{F}_0|_{\mathcal{F}_i}$ and the tordre for that it satisfies (ii).

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:3.3}
There exists a etale cover connected $q: Z' \to Z$ such that the group of monodromy of $q^*\mathcal{F}$ Let pro-$\ell$-group.
\end{lemma}

This which we importe is that the restriction of $q^*\mathcal{F}$ a curve tracee on $Z$ let moderement ramifiee a the infini.

\noindent\textit{Proof.} There exists a finite extension $E_\lambda$ of $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$, of ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_\lambda$, and a $\mathcal{O}_\lambda$-sheaf smooth without twisting $\tilde{\mathcal{F}}$ such that $\mathcal{F}$ let isomorphic a $\tilde{\mathcal{F}} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_\lambda} \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. The reduction of $\tilde{\mathcal{F}}$ modulo the ideal maximal $\mathfrak{m}_\lambda$ of $\mathcal{O}_\lambda$ is a sheaf étale locally constant, and it is enough to prendre for $Z'$ a covering of $Z$ on lequel it devienne constant. Si $\mathcal{F}$ is of rank $r$, one can prendre for $Z'$ a composante connected of the covering $\Isom(\tilde{\mathcal{F}}/\mathfrak{m}_\lambda\tilde{\mathcal{F}}, (\mathcal{O}_\lambda/\mathfrak{m}_\lambda)^r)$. On the covering $Z'$, the monodromy of each $\tilde{\mathcal{F}}/\mathfrak{m}_\lambda^n\tilde{\mathcal{F}}$ is a $\ell$-group.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:3.4}
Si the integer $n$ is sufficiently grand, for every $x \in Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, the trace $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ is contenue in the extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ generated by the traces $\tr(F_{y_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ with $y \in Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^m})$ and $m < n$.
\end{proposition}

Si $N$ is such that the integers $n > N$ let ``sufficiently grands'', one deduces by recurrence that every trace $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ is contenue in the extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ generated by the $\tr(F_{y_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ with $y$ in a $Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^m})$ with $m \leq N$. This extension is finite and \ref{prop:3.4} implique therefore \ref{thm:3.1}.

Let $x \in Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ and essayons of prouver the conclusion of \ref{prop:3.4} for $x$. One y arrivera for $n$ sufficiently grand.

Choisissons a generateur of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ on $\mathbb{F}_q$. This choix defines a $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$-point $x'$ of the line affine $\mathbb{A}_0^1$ on $\mathbb{F}_q$, of which the $\Gal(\mathbb{F}_{q^n}/\mathbb{F}_q)$-conjugues are all distincts.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:3.5}
Si $y$ is a $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$-point of $\mathbb{A}_0^1$, there exists a $\mathbb{F}_q$-morphism $P: \mathbb{A}_0^1 \to \mathbb{A}_0^1$, i.e. a polynome $P \in \mathbb{F}_q[T]$, which envoie $x'$ on $y$ and let of degree $\leq n-1$.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textit{Proof.} The $\sigma x'$, for $\sigma \in \Gal(\mathbb{F}_{q^n}/\mathbb{F}_q)$, are $n$ points distincts of the line affine. There exists therefore a unique polynome $P \in \mathbb{F}_{q^n}[T]$, of degree $\leq n-1$, which for each $\sigma$ prenne en $\sigma x'$ the value $\sigma y$. Son unicite assure son invariance by Galois, therefore that it is in $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$.

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:3.6}
There exists a $\mathbb{F}_q$-morphism $P: \mathbb{A}_0^1 \to \mathbb{A}_0^k$, of coordonnees of the polynomes of degree $\leq n-1$, which envoie $x' \in \mathbb{A}_0^1(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ on $\phi(x) \in \mathbb{A}_0^k(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$.
\end{corollary}

That se satisfies en appliquant \ref{lem:3.5} a each coordonnee of $\phi(x)$.

\subsection{3.7}

Fixons $P$ as en \ref{cor:3.6}. Let $X_0''$ the fiber product of $Z_0$ and $\mathbb{A}_0^1$ on $\mathbb{A}_0^k$. Puisque $\phi(x) = P(x')$, there exists $\bar{x} \in X_0''(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ s'envoyant on $x$ and $x'$. One denotes $X_0$ the composante connected of $X_0''$ contenant $\bar{x}$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:3.7.1}
\xymatrix{
X_0 \ar@{^{(}->}[r] & X_0'' \ar[r]^{\phi''} \ar[d]_{P} & \mathbb{A}_0^k \\
& \mathbb{A}_0^1 \ar[ur]_{P} &
}
\quad
\xymatrix{
\bar{x} \in X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n}) \ar@{|->}[d] \ar@{|->}[r] & x \in Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n}) \ar@{|->}[d] \\
x' \in \mathbb{A}_0^1(\mathbb{F}_{q^n}) \ar@{|->}[r] & \phi(x) \in \mathbb{A}_0^k(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})
}
\end{equation}
The morphism $\phi''$ is étale, of degree to the-dessus of the point generique of $\mathbb{A}_0^1$ to the more egal to the degree $D$ of $\phi$. Let $k_0$ the field of the constants of the curve $X_0$ on $\mathbb{F}_q$. The degree of $k_0$ on $\mathbb{F}_q$ is $\leq D$, car $X_0$ is of degree $\leq D$ on $\mathbb{A}_0^1$, and $d$ divise $n$, car $X_0$ a point on $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$. Etendons the field of base of $\mathbb{F}_q$ a $\mathbb{F}_{q^d}$, and let $X_1$ (resp.~$Z_1$) the composante connected of $X_0 \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q} \mathbb{F}_{q^d}$ (resp.~$Z_0 \otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q} \mathbb{F}_{q^d}$) which contient $\bar{x}$ (resp.~$x$):
\begin{equation}\label{eq:3.7.2}
\xymatrix{
\bar{x}: \Spec(\mathbb{F}_{q^n}) \ar[r] \ar[d] & X_1 \ar[r]^{\sim} \ar[d] & X_0 \ar[d]^{P} \\
x: \Spec(\mathbb{F}_{q^n}) \ar[r] & Z_1 \ar[r] & Z_0 \\
& \Spec(\mathbb{F}_{q^d}) \ar[r] & \Spec(\mathbb{F}_q)
}
\end{equation}
The curve $X_1$ on $\mathbb{F}_{q^d}$ is smooth and absolument irreducible. Etendons enfin the field of base of $\mathbb{F}_{q^d}$ a $\mathbb{F}$, for obtenir $X$ and $Z$, and let $X'$ a composante connected of the inverse image $X''$ of the etale cover $Z'$ of $Z$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:3.7.3}
\xymatrix{
X' \ar@{^{(}->}[r] & X'' \ar[r] & X \\
& Z' \ar[r] & Z
}
\end{equation}

\subsection{3.8}

Proof of \ref{prop:3.4}. the inverse image of $\mathcal{F}$ on $X'$ is moderement ramifiee. We we proposons of appliquer \ref{var:2.13} a the curve $X_1$ on $\mathbb{F}_{q^d}$, a $X' \to X$ and a the inverse image $\mathcal{F}_1$ of $\mathcal{F}_0$ on $X_1$. Estimons $b_1(X')$.

The $\mathbb{F}$-morphism compose
\[
Z' \to Z \to \mathbb{A}^k
\]
is affine. It se factorise therefore by a embedding closed $Z' \hookrightarrow \mathbb{A}^{k+k'}$, and there exists a family of $A$ equations of degree $\leq B$ definissant $Z'$ in $\mathbb{A}^{k+k'}$.

The graphe $\Gamma_P$ of $P: \mathbb{A}^1 \to \mathbb{A}^k$ is defined in $\mathbb{A}^{1+k}$ by $k$ equations of degree $\leq n-1$.

The fiber product, calcule on $\mathbb{F}$, of $Z' \to \mathbb{A}^k$ and $P: \mathbb{A}^1 \to \mathbb{A}^k$ is the intersection, in $\mathbb{A}^{1+k+k'}$, of the images inverses of $Z' \subset \mathbb{A}^{k+k'}$ and of $\Gamma_P \subset \mathbb{A}^{1+k}$. It is therefore defined, in $\mathbb{A}^{1+k+k'}$, by $A' := A+k$ equations of degree $\sup(B, n-1)$. of after Katz [K] this implique a majoration of the sum of the nombres of Betti of this fiber product, and a fortiori of $b_1(X')$, puisque $X'$ is a composante connected of the fiber product.

For $n > B$, one has $A'$ equations of degree $\leq n-1$ in a affine space a $k+k'+1$ dimensions, and Katz given
\begin{equation}\label{eq:3.8.1}
b_1(X') \leq 6.2 \cdot A' \cdot (A'n+3)^{k+k'+1}.
\end{equation}
Posons as en \ref{var:2.12}
\[
N'_0 = 2\log_{q^d}^+(2r^2 \cdot b_1(X')) \quad \text{et} \quad N' = [N'_0] + 2r.
\]
The borne (\ref{eq:3.8.1}) is polynomiale en $n$ and $d$ is borne by $D$. Of the that $n$ is sufficiently grand, one has therefore
\[
n > N' \cdot d.
\]
Supposons $n$ sufficiently grand for that this inegalite let verifiee.

By (\ref{eq:3.7.2}), one has $\tr(F_{\bar{x}}, \mathcal{F}_1) = \tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$. of after \ref{var:2.13}, this trace is contenue in the field generated by the $\tr(F_y, \mathcal{F}_1)$ for $y$ in a $X_1(\mathbb{F}_{q^m})$ with $d|m$ and $m/d$ to the more egal a $N'$. By (\ref{eq:3.7.2}) again, these traces are also the $\tr(F_{y_0}, P^*\mathcal{F}_0)$ for $y$ in a $X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^m})$ with $d|m$ and $m/d \leq N'$. one has
\[
\tr(F_{y_0}, P^*\mathcal{F}_0) = \tr(F_{P(y)_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)
\]
and $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ is in the field generated by the $\tr(F_{y_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ with $y \in Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^m})$ and $m/d \leq N'$, and therefore $m < n$. This proves \ref{prop:3.4}.

\begin{remark}\label{rem:3.9}
Si one ne assumed not $\mathcal{F}_0$ algebraic, it reste vrai that the extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ generated by the $\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0)$ for $x$ in a quelconque $Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ is a extension of type finite. One can the deduire by twisting of the cas algebraic, or repeter the arguments which precedent en appliquant \ref{rem:2.14}.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:3.10}
Sauf in the proof of \ref{lem:3.3}, nos arguments n'have utilise the sheaf $\mathcal{F}_0$ that via ses images inverses on of the curves smooth. The theorem \ref{thm:3.1} reste therefore valable si one se given, not not $\mathcal{F}_0$, but of the functions ``trace'' $t_n$ on the $Z_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, with values in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$, ayant the deux properties suivantes:

\emph{a.} For every curve smooth $X_0$ and all morphism $\phi: X_0 \to Z_0$, there exists a $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf smooth $\mathcal{F}_0[\phi]$ on $X_0$, such that for every $n$ and all $x \in X_0(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ one ait
\[
\tr(F_{x_0}, \mathcal{F}_0[\phi]) = t_n(\phi(x)).
\]

\emph{b.} There exists a etale cover connected $q: Z' \to Z$ such that for every $\phi: X_0 \to Z_0$ as en a., notant $X'$ the etale cover of $X_0$ inverse image of $Z'$, one ait: the inverse image of $\mathcal{F}_0[\phi]$ on $X'$ is moderement ramifiee a the infini.

the hypothese a. se substitue a \ref{lem:3.3}. The conclusion is that the values of the $t_n$ engendrent a extension of type finite of $\mathbb{Q}$ (a finite extension si the values of the $t_n$ are algebraic).
\end{remark}
